questions.q: What did Passepartout refuse to sell, even though he was starving?
choices: His shoes from Bombay
His watch
His French songbook
His travelling-bag
questions.evidence: He might, indeed, sell his watch; but he would have starved first.

questions.q: What was Passepartout's first plan for getting money?
choices: To sing French and English songs in the streets
To work as a porter carrying bags at the docks
To ask the French consul in Yokohama for a small loan
To sell mangoes and tea to the sailors in port
questions.evidence: He knew several French and English songs

questions.q: Why did Passepartout trade his clothes with the old-clothes dealer?
choices: His own clothes had been torn on the Carnatic
He was too well dressed for a street singer and needed money
The dealer said Europeans were not allowed in that quarter
He wanted to hide from Fix by dressing up and looking like a native
questions.evidence: he would seem rather too well dressed for a wandering artist

questions.q: What did Passepartout do right after changing his clothes?
choices: He went to the docks to look for work
He ate at a tea-house
He sang his first song in the market
He went to the theatre to buy a ticket
questions.evidence: upon half a bird and a little rice

questions.q: What did Passepartout plan to offer the American steamers in return for his passage?
choices: To work as a cook or servant
To pay them back once he reached San Francisco
To sing for the passengers every evening
To clean the decks and polish the brass
questions.evidence: He would offer himself as a cook or servant

questions.q: Why did his plan to work on a steamer start to seem difficult?
choices: He was dressed oddly and could give no references
The steamers had all left Yokohama the day before
He did not know how to cook any American food
He was afraid of the long voyage across the Pacific

questions.q: Why did the placard carried by the clown catch Passepartout's eye?
choices: It offered free food and lodging to anyone who joined the troupe
It said the troupe was about to leave for the United States
It showed a picture of a man who looked like Mr. Fogg
It asked for a strong man to carry the stage scenery
questions.evidence: PRIOR TO THEIR DEPARTURE TO THE UNITED STATES

questions.q: Why did Mr. Batulcar say he did not need a servant?
choices: He already had two servants, his own two strong arms
He said he could not afford to pay anyone any more wages this year
His acrobats did all the work for him
He did not trust anyone who was not Japanese
questions.evidence: holding out his two robust arms

questions.q: How did Mr. Batulcar know Passepartout was not Japanese?
choices: Passepartout showed him his French passport
He could see through the disguise right away
A clown in the troupe had seen him on the ship
Passepartout told him so as soon as he came in
questions.evidence: You are no more a Japanese than I am a monkey!

questions.q: What job did Mr. Batulcar give Passepartout?
choices: Ticket seller
Clown in the troupe
Cook for the troupe
Musician in the band

questions.q: The text says Passepartout's new job "was not a very dignified position." What does "dignified" mean?
choices: Paying a lot of money
Proper and worthy of respect
Safe and free from danger
Easy and not tiring
questions.evidence: It was not a very dignified position

questions.q: What were the Long Noses' noses made of?
choices: Bamboo
Paper
Clay
Leather
questions.evidence: These noses were made of bamboo

questions.q: Why was Passepartout chosen for the base of the "human pyramid"?
choices: He was the tallest man in the whole troupe
The usual base man had quit the troupe
Mr. Batulcar wanted the audience to laugh at a new clown
He had practised it for many years as a young gymnast
questions.evidence: the performer who had hitherto formed the base of the Car had quitted the troupe

questions.q: What made the human pyramid fall down?
choices: The orchestra's loud music shook the stage
Passepartout left his place to run to his master in the gallery
One of the bamboo noses snapped in two
A spectator threw something at the performers

questions.q: How did Fogg calm the furious Mr. Batulcar?
choices: He promised to pay him later in America
He gave him a handful of banknotes
He let Passepartout perform once more
He threatened to call the police
questions.evidence: Phileas Fogg appeased him by giving him a handful of banknotes

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Passepartout joins a troupe of acrobats in Yokohama and finds his master there
Fogg and Aouda search Yokohama for Passepartout with the help of the police
Passepartout gets a job as a cook on an American steamer
Fix catches Passepartout and makes him confess everything
